author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Jane Castor endorses Ken Welch in high-stakes St. Pete mayoral race
text:
Tampa Mayor Jane Castor announced on Apr. 29 her endorsement of St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch for re-election, providing a notable regional show of support as the city heads into a competitive mayoral race.
The endorsement comes shortly after former Governor Charlie Crist filed to run against Welch, joining several other candidates vying for the position in this year’s election. The contest has drawn attention due to its prominent participants and the issues at stake for St. Petersburg.
Castor said she has worked closely with Welch on regional issues and praised his leadership qualities. “Mayor Ken Welch has been a thoughtful, collaborative leader for St. Petersburg and a strong partner for our entire region,” Castor said. “He leads with integrity, puts people first, and understands how to bring communities together to get things done. St. Petersburg is stronger because of his leadership, and I’m proud to support his re-election.”
Welch faces multiple challengers from different backgrounds as the election approaches. City Council member Brandi Gabbard is supported by business interests and voters critical of Welch’s recent decisions regarding state-level policy disputes; former Fire Chief Jim Large brings decades of public service experience; Kevin Batdorf represents grassroots concerns about storm recovery; Maria Scruggs qualified by petition; while Crist enters with over $1 million raised through an affiliated committee.
Welch’s campaign continues to build support from labor groups, elected officials, and community leaders who cite his work on storm recovery, housing affordability, economic development, and redevelopment projects like the Historic Gas Plant District as reasons for their backing.
Welch expressed appreciation for Castor’s endorsement: “I’m grateful to Mayor Castor for her partnership and support,” he said. “The Tampa Bay region succeeds when we work together… As we look ahead, I’m focused on continuing to create opportunity, expand affordable housing, and ensure St. Petersburg remains a city where everyone can thrive.”
